added_failures_note: The reviewed run's manifest names no baseline_suite or after_suite, so I ran both arms at the pinned revisions on tests/discovery/ (the reviewed run's own adjacent selection). Base 1838c759f: 1473 passed, 3 deselected, EXIT=0 (logs/base_arm.log). Head 011d2445e: 1475 passed, 3 deselected, EXIT=0 (logs/head_arm.log). Head has no failures, so the change adds none; the +2 tests are the new file. Both arms imported their scratch tree's imas_codex (positive control: base parallel.py has 1 occurrence of the clear marker, head has 2).
call_sites: propagate_source_enrichment is defined in imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py and called from the enrichment worker path in the same module after the representative is enriched; individualize_source_descriptions is the existing pass it re-arms and is called once per discovery run after propagation.

findings.text: follow-on (evidence fidelity): the fragment and the manifest state twenty jt-60sa sources marked members_described whose members shared one description (1,324 members). My independent census at review time finds 89 such sources / 1,312 members. The member total agrees within 1 percent but the source count differs about 4.5x, which the stated definition does not explain; the graph is concurrently written so some difference is expected, but a source-count gap this large while members hold steady reads as an undercount in the reviewed census. It does not weaken the fix; the cause is corroborated more strongly.

follow-on (minor): the SET that clears members_described runs before the follower_count==0 early return, so a source with a single member also has its latch cleared. The individualization pass gates on size(members) > 1, so a singleton is never marked described again and the flag stays false. Harmless today because the pass skips it, but the second required test exercises only individualize_source_descriptions, not propagation, so the branch that fires the clear on a singleton is untested.

follow-on (durability): the _Graph mock recognises the production statements by literal Cypher substrings and the test keys the flag clear on the exact text sg.members_described = false being present in the SET. A rewrite of the propagation SET that preserved that substring but changed its semantics would leave the test green; the live graph read is what carries the end-to-end assurance.

(c) The census figure (twenty jt-60sa sources with members sharing one description, 1,324 members) is not reproducible: my independent census at review time finds 89 such sources / 1,312 members. The live artifact and the negative control are both confirmed.
justifications.fit: a single clause added to an existing SET that already carries sg.status, sg.description and sg.claimed_at, with a comment stating the mechanism; it re-arms the existing individualization pass rather than adding a second one, exactly as section 3 requires. Minimal and idiomatic.

justifications.reuse: reuses individualize_source_descriptions and the existing members_described latch rather than minting a parallel path; the only cost is that the latch now carries two meanings (never-described vs re-propagated), inherent to the design the plan fixed on.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff for 1838c759f..011d2445e lists exactly three paths -- imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py (modified), tests/discovery/test_source_individualization.py (added), docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-mapping-study-expansion/group-member-identity.html (added) -- exactly the manifest's declared write paths, with no generated model and nothing outside the fence.
